definitions.explanation: A verb that does not take a direct object. In Japanese grammar, intransitive verbs describe actions or states that happen on their own without an agent acting on something.

examples.japanese: 「⟦{開|あ}く→開く：00689_aku⟧」⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{自動詞|じどうし}です。
{自動詞|じどうし}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{目的語|もくてきご}→目的語：20479_mokutekigo⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}らない→取る：00565_toru⟧。
examples.english: Intransitive verbs do not take a direct object.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{自動詞|じどうし}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{他動詞|たどうし}→他動詞：10418_tadoushi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{区別|くべつ}→区別：01555_kubetsu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{大切|たいせつ}→大切：01456_taisetsu⟧です。
examples.english: In Japanese, the distinction between intransitive and transitive verbs is important.

notes:
COMMON PATTERNS:
Common pairs (intransitive / transitive):
- ⟦{開|あ}く→開く：00689_aku⟧ / ⟦{開|あ}ける→開ける：00563_akeru⟧ (open)
- ⟦{閉|し}まる→閉まる：00754_shimaru⟧ / ⟦{閉|し}める→閉める：00485_shimeru⟧ (close)
- ⟦{始|はじ}まる→始まる：00841_hajimaru⟧ / {始|はじ}める (begin)
- ⟦{壊|こわ}れる→壊れる：00791_kowareru⟧ / ⟦{壊|こわ}す→壊す：01241_kowasu⟧ (break)

In a sentence:
- Intransitive: ⟦ドア→ドア：00773_doa⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{開|あ}く→開く：00689_aku⟧ (the door opens — subject marked with が)
- Transitive: ⟦ドア→ドア：00773_doa⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|あ}ける→開ける：00563_akeru⟧ (open the door — object marked with ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧)

WATCH OUT:
- Some intransitive verbs of motion take ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧ for the path or the place left: ⟦{道|みち}→道：00505_michi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{歩|ある}く→歩く：00538_aruku⟧ (walk along the road), ⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{出|で}る→出る：00513_deru⟧ (leave the house). This ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧ is not a direct object, so the verbs are still {自動詞|じどうし}.
